lessons.title: Case Study: Switching Between Momentum and Mean Reversion on Nifty 50 Stocks

body.text: This case study puts the blending framework through the exact stretch of Indian market history this course keeps returning to, and answers a direct question: would it actually have helped during the period that broke the plain crossover system all the way back in Chapter 1?

children.text: Picture a systematic desk running the previous lesson's framework across a basket of large-cap Nifty 50 constituents spanning different sectors, banking names, IT names, and diversified conglomerates like Reliance, HDFC Bank, and Infosys. The specific stocks matter less here than the regime arc they all lived through together: the same COVID crash, recovery, and 2022 chop this course has used throughout.
Reading the Framework Across Five Periods

body.caption: The Chapter 5 framework applied across the familiar 2020 to 2022 regime arc (illustrative)

children.text: Comparing Against Chapter 1's Original Crossover System

Chapter 1's Lesson 1 tracked a pure 50/200-day crossover system's illustrative equity curve through this exact stretch, strong through 2020 and 2021, then whipsawed down through 2022's chop, ending the year at 129 against a starting-of-2022 value of 149. Rerun the same starting conditions with this chapter's regime-blended approach instead of pure momentum, and the two curves only diverge once the regime genuinely changes.

body.title: Illustrative: Pure Momentum (Chapter 1) vs Regime-Blended (This Chapter), Same Starting Path

body.text: Both series are illustrative constructions built to show the mechanism, not the output of an actual backtest on real stock data. This is a demonstration of how the framework is supposed to behave, not evidence that it works, which is precisely what Chapter 7 exists to establish properly.

children.text: The two curves are identical through Q4 2021, since 2020 and 2021's Calm Uptrend regime gives momentum a dominant weight in both approaches anyway. They diverge sharply from Q1 2022 onward, exactly where the regime read shifts to Volatile Whipsaw and then Range-Bound Chop. Pure momentum keeps trading its crossover signals at close to full size through the chop and pays for it with repeated false starts. The regime-blended approach shrinks total exposure through the Volatile Whipsaw stretch and shifts weight toward mean reversion through the Range-Bound Chop stretch, ending 2022 at 152 against pure momentum's 129, a roughly 23-point gap on the same starting conditions.

body.label: 2022 full-year outcome, same starting point of 149
body.context: The entire gap opens up during exactly the two periods, Volatile Whipsaw and Range-Bound Chop, that this chapter's framework was built to handle differently from a pure trend-following approach.

children.text: Two separate mechanisms contributed. First, the confidence-scaled exposure rule from the previous lesson cut total position size to 0.55 during the genuinely ambiguous Volatile Whipsaw stretch, so even the whipsawed trades that did occur were smaller and cost less. Second, the mean-reversion weight rising to 0.75 during the Range-Bound Chop stretch let the blended strategy actually profit from the oscillations that were pure cost for a trend-only approach, buying into the dips and selling into the bounces of a market with no real sustained direction, exactly the behavior Chapter 1's Lesson 1 originally described mean reversion as suited for.

body.title: Identifying the Source of the Improvement
body.question: In this case study, the regime-blended approach and the pure momentum approach produce identical results through Q4 2021 and only diverge starting in 2022. Why?
options: The regime-blended approach uses different price data starting in 2022
The Calm Uptrend regime through 2020 and 2021 gives momentum a dominant weight under both approaches, so the blend behaves almost like pure momentum until the regime actually changes
The two approaches always produce identical results and the 2022 divergence is a modeling error
Mean reversion only exists as a strategy starting in 2022
body.explanation: The blending framework does not create a difference out of nothing; it only changes behavior when P(trend) meaningfully departs from a clean trending regime. Through 2020 and 2021, P(trend) stays high enough that momentum dominates the blend almost as much as it would a pure momentum strategy. The real test of the framework only arrives once the regime genuinely shifts, which is exactly the 2022 stretch this case study focuses on.

body.title: Stress-Testing the Case Study's Honesty
body.scenario: A colleague reviewing this case study says: 'Great, this proves regime-blending beats pure momentum. Let's size up and run it live.'
body.prompt: What is wrong with drawing that conclusion directly from this lesson's chart, and what would need to happen before this framework should be trusted with real capital?
body.modelAnswer: This case study is an illustrative demonstration of the mechanism, built by hand to show how the framework is supposed to behave in the regimes it targets, not a real backtest on actual price data with real transaction costs, real regime detection lag, and real out-of-sample testing. It proves the logic is internally coherent, not that it produces genuine alpha. Before trusting it with capital, the framework needs a proper walk-forward backtest on real data as covered in Chapter 7, explicit accounting for the detection lag between when a regime actually shifts and when the fitted model recognizes it, and validation that the momentum and mean-reversion sub-strategies themselves have a real edge before the blending layer is even added on top.

points: Applying the Chapter 5 framework across the familiar 2020 to 2022 regime arc shows it behaves almost identically to pure momentum during a clean, confirmed uptrend, since P(trend) stays high
The framework only meaningfully diverges from a pure momentum approach once the regime genuinely shifts away from trending, exactly where it is designed to help

In this illustrative case study, confidence-scaled exposure reduction during Volatile Whipsaw and increased mean-reversion weight during Range-Bound Chop together produce a roughly 23-point gap over pure momentum by the end of 2022

The improvement traces to two distinct mechanisms: smaller position sizes during genuine uncertainty, and genuine mean-reversion profits captured during a directionless stretch that pure momentum could only lose money in

This case study demonstrates the framework's logic, not its real-world edge; Chapter 7's backtesting discipline is required before any of these numbers should be treated as evidence rather than illustration
